factual_summaries.summary: Google announced support for Agent Plugins 1.0.0, a vendor-neutral package format combining Agent Skills and MCP servers with a fixed directory layout and plugin manifest; Google joined the core maintainer group and shipped support through Agents CLI and Data Agent Kit.
Vercel announced Agent Plugins 1.0.0 as a small vendor-neutral packaging format with plugin.json, fixed component locations, published schemas, guides, and GitHub-hosted governance.
GitHub announced Agent Plugins 1.0 support in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app, including marketplace installation and shared plugin packages across compatible clients.

GitHub Copilot updates included session resume and organization improvements, shared-session jumps, side questions, model/credit/cache visibility for completed requests, and a design-review skill update.
GitHub made Lite and Balanced Copilot code review effort levels generally available, with per-review selection and organization-level defaults for review depth.
GitHub added third-party agent app activity to the Copilot usage metrics API, broken out by individual recognized agent in 1-day and 28-day reports.
GitHub added a potential ROI section to the Copilot impact dashboard that relates Copilot spend and AI credit consumption to pull-request output and developer compensation assumptions.

Business Insider reported a shift from chatbot-response training toward reinforcement learning environments that simulate workplace tasks, including software engineering, enterprise software use, and long-running work; it also described Uber Agentic Pods observing and redesigning department workflows.
daily.dev compared major coding agents and argued teams should choose based on autonomy, reliability, price, workflow fit, and review capacity rather than a single best-agent ranking.
